target.title: test: cover ClickClack tail cursor fallback
target.body:
Related: #102486
Related: openclaw/clickclack#46

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a regression-test gap around the ClickClack startup tail-cursor approach that landed after #102486 was reworked before merge.

The merged implementation now depends on a ClickClack server-captured `tail_cursor`, with an old-server fallback when that field is absent. This adds coverage for both the fallback branch and malformed `tail_cursor` parsing so future edits do not quietly reopen startup backlog replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a tests-only follow-up to the maintainer-adjusted approach: keep the server-captured startup tail as the preferred path, preserve old-server behavior when `tail_cursor` is omitted, and ignore malformed non-string `tail_cursor` values at the HTTP client boundary.

AI-assisted. Authored by ragesaq; code by Chisel; model `openai/gpt-5.5`.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Maintainers get focused regression coverage for the ClickClack startup subscription contract and its compatibility fallback.

## Evidence

Validation run on branch `ragesaq/clickclack-tail-cursor-tests` at `f892850c26b1bf0b61b6c1c68d67af893fa0a927`:

```text
pnpm test:extension clickclack
Test Files  8 passed (8)
Tests       64 passed (64)

pnpm tsgo:extensions
passed

pnpm check:bundled-channel-config-metadata
passed

git diff --check
passed
```

`codex review --base origin/main` could not complete in this local environment because the Codex CLI is not authenticated; it failed with `401 Unauthorized: Missing bearer or basic authentication` on both websocket and HTTPS transports.

Anvil final gate: GREEN on exact head `f892850c26b1bf0b61b6c1c68d67af893fa0a927`.

Anvil also mutation-checked both new tests:

- changing the old-server fallback to use the first startup event cursor failed exactly the new gateway test;
- accepting numeric `tail_cursor` values failed exactly the new HTTP client test.
